h1: Urgent Indian e-Visa from the UK: how fast can you get one?
intro: Need an urgent Indian e-Visa? If your arrival in India is at least 4 days away, you can still apply, and most decisions arrive by email within 72 hours. Here’s exactly what’s possible, what it costs a British passport holder, and what to do if time has already run out.

sections.heading: Can you get an urgent Indian e-Visa?
sections.text:
Yes, as long as you apply at least 4 days before you arrive in India. The Government of India aims to decide e-Visa applications within 72 hours, and many straightforward ones come back sooner.

What you can’t do is pay for a faster decision. There is one official processing track for every applicant. Any website selling a guaranteed same-day or “super rush” Indian e-Visa is charging you for something the government doesn’t offer.

So when you need an urgent Indian e-Visa, speed comes from one thing: sending a complete, correct application the first time, so it isn’t sent back.

sections.heading: The 4-day rule for an urgent Indian e-Visa
sections.text:
These rules decide whether you fly on time:

- Apply at least 4 days before your arrival date. The online form won’t accept a closer date.
- Pay the government fee at least 4 days before travel. Unpaid applications aren’t processed.
- Allow up to 4 hours for your payment to register. Don’t submit a second application while you wait.
- Land at an [approved airport or seaport](/indian-visa-application-uk/). e-Visa holders can’t enter India by land.

Count the days to your arrival in India, not your departure from the UK. A night flight from Manchester or London can land a day later.

sections.heading: Urgent Indian e-Visa fees for British citizens
sections.text:
The Government of India charges British passport holders these e-Visa fees, set in US dollars. There’s no extra fee for urgent applications.

- e-Tourist visa, 30 days, arriving July to March: US$25
- e-Tourist visa, 30 days, arriving April to June: US$10
- e-Tourist visa, 1 year: US$40
- e-Tourist visa, 5 years: US$484
- e-Business visa: US$242
- e-Medical and e-Medical Attendant visas: US$129 each

A bank charge of about 3% is added for card payments. Your bank converts the fee to pounds on the day. The fee isn’t refunded if the visa is refused, so it pays to get the application right. See the official [e-Tourist fee table](https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/images/Etourist_fee_final.pdf) and [e-Business and e-Medical fee table](https://indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/images/eTV_revised_fee_final.pdf), or read our guide to [Indian e-Visa fees](/indian-visa-application-uk/).

For a single urgent trip, the 30-day or 1-year e-Tourist visa is almost always better value than the 5-year visa at UK rates.

sections.heading: What slows an urgent application down
sections.text:
When time is short, a request to resubmit can cost you the trip. These are the problems we see most:

- A photo with shadows, glasses or a background that isn’t plain white. Check the [photo rules](/visa-photo-tool/).
- A passport scan where the two lines of code at the bottom are cut off or blurred.
- Less than six months left on your passport from your arrival date, or fewer than two blank pages.
- The wrong visa type, such as a tourist e-Visa for a business meeting.
- Names, dates or passport numbers that don’t match your passport exactly.
- Leaving out a previous visa refusal, or a wrong answer to the family background questions.

If you’ve had a refusal before, read [why Indian e-Visas get refused](/blog/why-indian-e-visas-get-refused/) before you apply again.

sections.heading: Which e-Visa to choose when you’re in a hurry
sections.text:
Pick the visa that matches the main reason for your trip:

- Family visits, holidays, weddings and funerals: [e-Tourist visa](/e-tourist-visa-india/)
- Meetings, site visits, trade fairs and sales trips: [e-Business visa](/e-business-visa-india/)
- Treatment at an Indian hospital: [e-Medical visa](/e-medical-visa-india/), with a letter from the hospital

See [every Indian e-Visa type](/indian-visa-application-uk/) if your trip doesn’t fit these.

sections.heading: Less than 4 days to go? The emergency visa route
sections.text:
If you need to arrive in India sooner than an urgent Indian e-Visa allows, there is one other option. The [High Commission of India in London](https://www.hcilondon.gov.in/page/emergency-visa/) can issue an emergency visa, but only for the death or serious illness of an immediate family member in India.

You fill in the regular visa form online, then apply in person at the High Commission in London or the Consulates in Birmingham or Edinburgh. You’ll need a death certificate or hospital letter from India, stamped, plus proof of your relationship. The fee is higher than an e-Visa and is paid in cash.

Weddings, engagements and religious events don’t count as emergencies. British citizens of Pakistani origin also can’t use the e-Visa and need a [regular visa](/indian-visa-application-uk/).

sections.heading: After you get your urgent Indian e-Visa
sections.text:
- Print the approval email or save it on your phone. Airlines check it before you board.
- Complete the free [India e-Arrival card](/blog/india-e-arrival-card-explained/) online in the 72 hours before you land.
- Carry the same passport you applied with.

If your approval hasn’t arrived after 72 hours, check your spam folder, then contact the official e-Visa helpline on +91 11 2430 0666.

sections.heading: How our Manchester team helps with an urgent Indian e-Visa
sections.text:
We can’t make the Government of India decide faster, and nobody honestly can. What we do is make sure your application is right the first time:

- We tell you straight away whether an e-Visa still works for your dates.
- We check and fix your photo and passport scan before anything is submitted.
- We choose the right e-Visa type and complete the official form for you.
- If you need the emergency route, we help you prepare the paperwork.

Travelling soon? [Start your Indian e-Visa application](/apply/india-visa/) or [contact us](/contact-us/) with your travel date.

faqs.q: Can I pay extra for an urgent Indian e-Visa?
faqs.a: No. The Government of India has one processing track and no express fee. Most decisions arrive within 72 hours.

faqs.q: How late can I apply for an urgent Indian e-Visa?
faqs.a: At least 4 days before you arrive in India. If your arrival is sooner, the e-Visa isn’t available.

faqs.q: How much is an Indian e-Visa for British citizens?
faqs.a: US$25 for a 30-day e-Tourist visa (US$10 if arriving April to June), US$40 for 1 year, US$484 for 5 years, US$242 for e-Business and US$129 for e-Medical, plus about 3% card charges.

faqs.q: I fly in 2 days. What can I do?
faqs.a: An e-Visa isn’t possible. If an immediate family member in India has died or is seriously ill, apply for an emergency visa at the High Commission of India or a Consulate. Otherwise, move your flight.

faqs.q: Does a wedding count as an emergency?
faqs.a: No. Emergency visas are only for the death or serious illness of an immediate family member.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa if I have an OCI card?
faqs.a: No. A valid OCI card lets you travel to India without a visa, with the passport linked to it.

title: Urgent Indian e-Visa from the UK: 4-Day Rule & Fees 2026
description: Need an urgent Indian e-Visa? The 4-day rule, 72-hour processing, 2026 fees for British citizens and the emergency visa route if time has run out.
